ety.text: 1950, from on + line.

senses.d: Of a generator or power plant: connected to the grid.
Of a computer: actively connected to the Internet or to some other communications service.
ex: Is this modem online?

senses.d: Available over, or delivered from, the Internet.
ex: I prefer to read online newspapers.
The online world was meant to be an open system but has become dominated by huge corporations.

senses.d: Connected to the Internet.
ex: I'll be online tonight, so I'll be able to reply to your email.

senses.d: Available on a computer system, even if not networked.
ex: Press the F1 key to access the online help.
The program comes with an online manual, supplied on compact disc.

senses.d: Of a system: active, particularly building facilities (such as power) or a factory or power plant.
ex: The power is online.
Once this factory comes online, it will double car production in our country!

senses.d: Immersed in Internet culture. (Usually modified by an intensifier such as extremely or terminally)
ex: terminally online
To borrow an idiom from the extremely online, late Godard is a mood.

senses.d: Able to process an input piece-by-piece without needing to have the entire input available to it from the start.
While online; while in a running or active state, or connected to the Internet.
ex: He works online.

senses.d: To bring (a system, etc.) online; to promote to an active or running state.

grp.label: of a system that is active

From Middle English oonly, only, from Old English ānlīċ, ǣnlīċ (“only; singular; solitary”), from Proto-Germanic *ainalīkaz. Cognate with obsolete Dutch eenlijk, German ähnlich (“similar”), Old Norse álíkr, Swedish enlig (“unified”). By surface analysis, on(e) + -ly. * Regarding the different phonological development of only and one, see the note in one.

senses.d: Alone in a category.
ex: He is the only doctor for miles.
The only people in the stadium were the fans: no players, coaches, or officials.

senses.d: Singularly superior; the best.
ex: Motley's the only wear.
"People say there's other games," Jack had said to Cassie at Small Falls earlier that day. "But baseball's the only game."

senses.d: Without sibling; without a sibling of the same gender.
ex: He is their only son, in fact, an only child.
To DAD ¶ who only reared twelve children ¶ and ¶ To MOTHER ¶ who reared twelve only children

senses.d: Mere.
Without others or anything further; exclusively.
ex: My heart is hers, and hers only.
I threw out only him.

senses.d: No more than; just.
ex:
To DAD
who only reared twelve children
and
To MOTHER
who reared twelve only children
The cat only sat on the mat. It didn't scratch it.

senses.d: As recently as.
ex:
c. 1924-1955, anonymous, The Urantia Book
Only yesterday did I feed you with bread for your bodies; today I offer you the bread of life for your hungry souls.
He left only moments ago.

senses.d: Emphasizing something that is just or necessary.
ex: It's only fair to let him borrow your kite, after you've had his toys all day.
He'd been belittling her for years. It's only natural that she left.

senses.d: Used to express surprise or consternation at an action.
ex: She's only gone and run off with the milkman!

senses.d: Just, simply, undoubtedly.
ex: Sure you're only gorgeous!

senses.d: Introduces a disappointing or surprising outcome that renders futile something previously mentioned.
ex: They rallied from a three-goal deficit only to lose in the final two minutes of play.
I spent years studying a degree only to learn there was no requirement for such a certification.

senses.d: Above all others; particularly.
ex: his most only elected mistress

senses.d: Under the condition that; but.
ex: You're welcome to borrow my bicycle, only please take care of it.

senses.d: But, except; but in fact.
ex: I would enjoy running, only I have this broken leg.
She would get good results only she gets nervous.

senses.d: An only child.
ex: Sometimes, secondborns marry onlys and the conflicts are similar.

senses.d: Placed at the end of a sentence to emphasize that something is trivial, small, undemanding or deserving of belittlement.
ex: Just need to replace the filter only.
